title: Exponential rule
text: An antiderivative of $$e^{k x}$$ is $$\frac{e^{k x}}{k}$$, and an antiderivative of $$a^x$$ is $$\frac{a^x}{\ln\left(a\right)}$$.

title: Apply
text: Write $$3^{\left(-x\right)}=e^{\left(-x \ln\left(3\right)\right)}$$. An antiderivative is $$\frac{e^{\left(-x \ln\left(3\right)\right)}}{\left(-\ln\left(3\right)\right)}$$, so the answer is $$\frac{-3^{\left(-x\right)}}{\ln\left(3\right)}+C$$.
